newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts tumbles on extortion threat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts tumbles on extortion threat.

text.p: Shares in Australia's largest biscuit-maker Arnotts Ltd fell 35 cents or four percent to A$8.40 in early afternoon trade after the lifting of a trading halt.

The company requested the trading half after news emerged that an extortionist had threatened to poison Arnotts' biscuits from Monday if police involved in the investigation of a 1991 murder case did not undergo lie detector tests.
Arnotts has responded by ordering that its entire product range be removed from supermarket shelves in New South Wales and Queensland.
Arnotts also made a preliminary release of its first half year results, showing a 14.2 percent fall in net profit pre-abnormals to A$33.2 million for the six months to January 24.
Arnotts also declared a 12 cent interim dividend.
Arnotts' net profit after abnormals fell to A$8.5 million from A$38.7 million in the same period a year earlier.
It also said the extortion threat placed a cloud over the future outlook for the company's earnings.
Volume was slight at 2,020 in early trade after the halt was lifted.
Arnotts is about 70 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co of the United States.
